security_audit.summary: Most scanner matches are false positives caused by animation terminology, Markdown backticks, CSS, relative asset paths, and test code. Confirmed risks are remote CDN execution and the package bootstrap chain, especially its mutable @latest fallback and dynamic import with inherited environment access. Static review was capped at 400/589 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 189 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The bootstrap fallback treats @latest as a pinned package version.
remediation.suggestion: Require an exact immutable version and refuse bootstrap when the bundled version cannot be determined.

remediation.issue: Bootstrapped package code runs in a process that inherits the full environment.
remediation.suggestion: Launch the imported tooling with a minimal environment and an explicit allowlist of required variables.

remediation.issue: Examples execute third-party CDN scripts without integrity metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Vendor browser dependencies or use exact versions with Subresource Integrity and a restrictive Content Security Policy.

content.value_statement: Complex motion scenes are hard to keep deterministic and seek-safe. This skill provides reusable HyperFrames rules, blueprints, transitions, adapters, and choreography auditing.
actual_capabilities: Selects atomic animation rules by trigger, visual role, and motion pattern.
Provides multi-phase blueprints for product scenes, brand reveals, data visuals, and interface demonstrations.
Explains GSAP, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS, WAAPI, and TypeGPU integration patterns.
Applies seek-safe timeline constraints for deterministic HyperFrames rendering.
Audits GSAP compositions by sampling tweens, identifying choreography issues, and writing an animation map.
Maps text needs to named animation effects and suitable scene transitions.
limitations: The guidance assumes the HyperFrames composition contract and related core conventions.
The animation-map script requires Node.js and the @hyperframes/producer package.
Many examples load browser libraries from remote CDNs and require network access.
The skill does not create original video, font, Lottie, or three-dimensional source assets.

use_cases.title: Compose Product Motion
use_cases.description: Combine atomic rules and scene blueprints into a deterministic product demonstration.

use_cases.title: Implement Web Animation
use_cases.description: Choose a supported runtime and build seekable timelines that match HyperFrames rendering constraints.

use_cases.title: Audit Choreography
use_cases.description: Generate an animation map to review tween timing, dead zones, collisions, and element lifecycles.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Animation Rule
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to animate [element] when [trigger] occurs. Recommend two suitable HyperFrames rules and explain the motion sequence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner selection of an atomic motion pattern

prompt_templates.title: Build a Scene Blueprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [duration]-second HyperFrames scene for [message]. Choose a blueprint, divide it into phases, and list the rules used.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a multi-phase scene

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a Runtime
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement this motion plan with [GSAP, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS, WAAPI, or TypeGPU]. Keep the result deterministic and seek-safe.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Full Composition
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the animation map for [composition]. Identify timing gaps, collisions, weak staggers, lifecycle problems, and concrete choreography improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert review of an existing composition

output_examples.input: Animate six feature cards into a product overview.
output_examples.output: Use the grid-card-assemble blueprint. Stagger short slide-and-fade entrances, hold the resolved grid, then transition focus to the primary card.
Use Three.js for the device and a single paused HyperFrames timeline. Drive camera, object transforms, and mixer time from deterministic seek values.

output_examples.input: Review an animation map with a long empty interval.
output_examples.output: The map shows a choreography dead zone. Extend the preceding settle, move the next entrance earlier, or add a purposeful focus transition.

best_practices: Compose two to four atomic rules before choosing a larger blueprint.
Use one paused timeline and precomputed layout values for deterministic seeking.
Pin dependencies locally and review animation-map findings after implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not build timelines inside asynchronous callbacks or wall-clock events.
Do not use unseeded randomness, infinite repeats, or user-event state during rendering.
Do not mix several runtimes unless each one has a clear scene responsibility.

faq.question: What is this skill designed for?
faq.answer: It supports deterministic motion design and implementation for HyperFrames compositions.

faq.question: Is GSAP required?
faq.answer: No. GSAP is the default, but the skill also covers Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS, WAAPI, and TypeGPU.

faq.question: Can it create complete scene plans?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides multi-phase blueprints and helps combine them with atomic rules and transitions.

faq.question: What does the animation-map script produce?
faq.answer: It writes an animation map with sampled tweens, element states, timing density, dead zones, staggers, collisions, and summaries.

faq.question: Does the skill work without network access?
faq.answer: Most guidance is local, but many examples use CDN libraries. The audit script may also bootstrap a missing package.

faq.question: Does it replace HyperFrames core guidance?
faq.answer: No. It depends on the HyperFrames core composition contract and adds animation-specific patterns.
